description: 2 tactical challenges for White against the Icelandic Gambit. Accept the pawn with 4.dxe6 and meet Black's initiative with the solid 5.Nf3.

drills.briefExplanation: 3.c4 e6 4.dxe6 Bxe6 5.Nf3 — accept the pawn, then develop before Black's initiative can grow.
drills.description: White to play. Black has played the modern 2...Nf6 — push 3.c4 and be ready for the Icelandic 3...e6.
drills.explanation: 3.c4 is White's most ambitious reply to 2...Nf6, and after 3...e6 White should accept: 4.dxe6 Bxe6. The key is not to get greedy — 5.Nf3 develops and prepares to castle, meeting Black's activity with solid development. White's extra pawn will tell in the endgame if Black's attack comes to nothing.
drills.name: Meeting the Icelandic

drills.briefExplanation: 5.Nf3 Nc6 6.Be2 Bc5 7.O-O — the critical test: develop, castle, and let the extra pawn speak.
drills.description: White to play. The pawn is accepted and Black's bishops are active — play the critical 5.Nf3.
drills.explanation: 5.Nf3 is the move that asks the Icelandic Gambit its hardest question: where is the compensation? After 5...Nc6 6.Be2 Bc5 White simply castles — 7.O-O — and Black's initiative has no target. The e6 bishop looks pretty but bites on granite; White will consolidate with Nc3, d3, and the extra pawn.
drills.name: The Critical Nf3
